```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
# Bash chunks are a record of commands you ran in the Terminal. Knitting shows
# them but doesn't run them again.
knitr::opts_hooks$set(engine = function(options) {
  if (options$engine == "bash") options$eval <- FALSE
  options
})
```

Notes for [Workshop 1](https://mb5370.bioinformatics.guide/workshop1.html). 
Run the commands for this workshop in the Terminal, from inside the `command_line` folder:

```{bash}
cd command_line
pwd
```

## Basic unix commands
pwd - print working directory e.g., /home/jc982704/mb5370-workshops
root directory always /

ls - list all files and folders in directory

unix command format: command, flag, directory
e.g., 
```{bash}
grep '^>' test.fasta.         #find fasta header
grep KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta    #specified search
grep -n KDRNKKNSAK test.fasta #line number included

man grep
```
where:
grep (globally search a regular expression and print) 
KDRNKKNSAK (specific amino acid sequence)
test.fasta (input directory i.e. file/folder)

fasta header - single-line description/definition line that begins a sequence entry, always begins with ">" followed be Sequence Identifier (SeqID) e.g.,num/chr

Examples of grep flags:

"-i" -> case insensitive match

"-n" -> report line number of matches

"-c" -> report all files that contain the pattern

"-w" -> match whole words only

## Viewing and searching files
```{bash}
cd ~/mb5370-workshops/command_line
echo $'>fasta_header\nMMGTSRCVILLFALLLWAANAAPPEIHTTRPNVPEEIKRPNSTEIETPAVKQLETPSIFL\nLTTLEVAEADVDSTLETMKDRNKKNSAKLSKIGNNMKSLLSVFSVFGGFLSLLSVVTTTS' > test.fasta

cat test.fasta
head -2 test.fasta

man cat
man head
```
man - - an interface to the system reference manuals
cat - concatenate files and print on the standard output
head - output the first part of files, can be specified with # 
e.g., -2 for only first 2 lines
 
## Sequence file formats

FASTA: used as "reference" data, no quality scores (assumes to be correct)
Used for wide variety of sequence types including whole genomes, transcriptomes, nucleotide and proteins
Format considers 1 or more entries each with a header/title line and sequence
Multiple entries can be stored in a single file
>SeqID base_sequence_lines

FASTQ: used for "raw" reads from next generation sequencing experiments, includes a quality score for every base
Used for Illumina short reads and longer reads by Nanopore or PacBio sequencing
Format designed for storing sequencing data along quality scores in 4 lines 
@SeqID base_sequence_line + Description and Quality Score lines

1. Starts with @ and contains a unique identifier for the sequence
2. Is the sequence itself
3. Starts with + and almost always nothing else
4. Contains quality scores. These are encoded using ASCII characters with one character per base.

```{bash}
#Full list of quality score letters from 0-94
!\"#$%&\'()*+,-./0123456789:;<=>?@ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ[\]^_\`abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz{|}~
```
